title: Accept query-bound artifact checksums from older ticket issuers
description:
Artifact uploads fail when an older deployed ticket issuer returns x-amz-checksum-sha256 as a required header even though the presigned URL already binds that checksum in its query and does not include the header in X-Amz-SignedHeaders. The shared client must normalize only this provably duplicated checksum representation and retain fail-closed behavior for every other unsigned or contradictory header.

Feature: Compatible artifact transfer tickets

Scenario: Query-bound checksum is redundantly returned as an unsigned header
  Given a PUT ticket whose URL contains X-Amz-Checksum-Sha256
  And X-Amz-SignedHeaders does not contain x-amz-checksum-sha256
  And requiredHeaders contains the identical x-amz-checksum-sha256 value
  When the shared artifact client transfers the authorized bytes
  Then it omits only the redundant checksum header
  And preserves every signed and ordinary required header

Scenario: Checksum evidence is inconsistent
  Given a checksum header that is signed, absent from the URL, or differs from the URL value
  When the shared artifact client validates the ticket
  Then it does not silently discard the header
  And the transfer continues to fail closed if authorization rejects it

comments.author: ryan.porter
comments.text: Production acceptance reproduced the failure with a real ticket. The ticket URL carried the checksum in its query, X-Amz-SignedHeaders contained only content-length and host, and requiredHeaders redundantly included x-amz-checksum-sha256. S3 returned AccessDenied because that header was present but unsigned. No optimizer or report run proceeded past procedure-code publication.
